Pilocarpine is used as a sialogogue in the treatment of dry mouth (p.2140) after radiotherapy of the head and neck,1,2 although benefit may not be entirely related to preservation of salivation.3,4 A systematic review5 based on 3 studies found lim- ited evidence to support such use; although about half of the pa- tients responded to pilocarpine, response did not occur in some for up to 12 weeks and adverse effects were common. Pilo- carpine may also be of use in the management of drug-induced oral dryness,6 and is used as a treatment for dry mouth and dry eye in the auto-immune disease, Sjögren’s syndrome.1,7-10 1.
